app.name: Desktop
app.subtitle: window look and behaviour
sec.appearance.d: Gaps, borders, transparency, blur, shadows and animations.
sec.windows.d: How windows are arranged, moved and focused.
sec.changes.d: What you are about to change, before applying it.
o.general:gaps_out.d: Pixels between windows and the screen edge.
o.general:border_size.d: Coloured line around each window (0 = no border).
o.decoration:rounding.d: Corner radius in pixels (0 = square corners).
o.decoration:rounding_power.d: 2 = circle; higher values give squarer, smoother corners.
o.decoration:active_opacity.d: 1 = fully opaque; lower lets you see what is behind.
o.decoration:inactive_opacity.d: Transparency of the windows you are not using.
o.decoration:dim_inactive.d: Helps you see at a glance which window you are using.
o.decoration:dim_special.d: Darkens the background when the special workspace (scratchpad) opens.
o.decoration:blur:enabled.d: What shows through a transparent window looks frosted.
o.decoration:blur:passes.d: More passes look smoother but use more GPU.
o.decoration:blur:vibrancy.d: Saturates the colours of the blurred background.
o.decoration:blur:xray.d: Floating windows show the wallpaper instead of the windows below.
o.decoration:blur:ignore_opacity.d: Blur does not depend on the window's transparency.
o.decoration:shadow:enabled.d: Draws a soft shadow around each window.
o.decoration:shadow:range.d: How far the shadow reaches, in pixels.
o.decoration:shadow:sharp.d: Shadow with a hard edge, no blur.
o.animations:enabled.d: Transitions when opening, closing and moving windows. Turn off on slow computers.
o.x:anim_windows.d: Effect used when windows appear and disappear.
o.animations:workspace_wraparound.d: When going from the last workspace to the first, keep the animation direction.
o.general:layout.d: How new windows are placed on screen.
o.dwindle:force_split.d: In spiral tiling: which side of the current window the new one appears.
o.dwindle:preserve_split.d: The horizontal or vertical split stays when resizing.
o.dwindle:smart_split.d: Splits the window based on where the mouse is inside it.
o.dwindle:smart_resizing.d: When resizing, the edge that moves depends on the mouse position.
o.dwindle:default_split_ratio.d: 1 = half and half; other values favour one side.
o.master:mfact.d: In “main window and stack”: how much of the screen the main window takes.
o.master:orientation.d: In “main window and stack”: where the main window goes.
o.master:new_status.d: In “main window and stack”: whether a new window becomes the main one.
o.scrolling:column_width.d: In “scrolling columns”: fraction of the screen each column takes.
o.general:resize_on_border.d: Drag a window's border with the mouse to resize it.
o.general:extend_border_grab_area.d: Extra pixels around the border you can grab.
o.general:hover_icon_on_border.d: Shows the resize cursor when hovering a border.
o.general:snap:enabled.d: Floating windows stick to other windows and the screen edges.
o.general:snap:window_gap.d: How many pixels away from another window it snaps.
o.general:snap:monitor_gap.d: How many pixels away from the screen edge it snaps.
o.general:snap:border_overlap.d: Snapped windows share their border instead of sitting side by side.
o.misc:animate_manual_resizes.d: Animates resizing done with the mouse or keyboard.
o.misc:animate_mouse_windowdragging.d: Animates windows while you drag them with the mouse.
o.x:ws_persistent.d: How many workspaces exist even when empty (0 = only the ones in use, like Omarchy).
o.binds:workspace_back_and_forth.d: Pressing the shortcut of the current workspace takes you to the previous one.
o.binds:allow_workspace_cycles.d: “Previous workspace” always toggles between the last two.
o.binds:hide_special_on_workspace_change: The special workspace (scratchpad) closes when switching workspaces.
o.misc:focus_on_activate: Focus windows that ask for it
o.misc:focus_on_activate.d: When an app asks for attention (e.g. opening a link), jump to its window.
o.misc:on_focus_under_fullscreen.d: What happens when a window opens while another is fullscreen.
o.general:no_focus_fallback.d: Moving focus towards an empty side doesn't jump to another monitor.
o.general:allow_tearing.d: Less latency in games at the cost of possible image tearing. Only for games that request it.
o.group:groupbar:enabled.d: Shows a tab bar above grouped windows.
o.group:groupbar:font_size.d: Text size on the tab bar.
o.group:groupbar:gradients.d: Draws a coloured background behind each tab.
note.no_gaps: Omarchy's “no gaps” mode is on (Menu → Trigger → Toggle): while it is, gaps, borders and corners are 0.
note.meca: Meca HyprConfig is still active and loads after Desktop: its values override these. This stays until Desktop replaces it.
note.foreign: escritorio.lua was not created by this tool; applying will replace it (with a backup).
note.offline: Hyprland was not detected: Omarchy's values are shown and changes will be used at next login.
note.base: Anything you don't change here follows Omarchy and your own files (looknfeel.lua, input.lua…).
cli.about: TUI panel to configure the look and behaviour of Hyprland windows on Omarchy.
cli.section: open a section directly: appearance, windows, monitors, keyboard, mouse, cursor, keybinds, autostart, night, compose, screenshots, changes
msg.applied: Changes applied ✓ Hyprland is using them.
msg.applied_offline: Changes saved. They will be used when Hyprland starts.
msg.applied_sandbox: Changes saved in the test folder.
msg.rolled_back: Hyprland rejected the configuration, so nothing was saved:
restore.section.desc: This screen's settings go back to Omarchy's values.
restore.all.desc: All Desktop settings are removed: everything goes back to Omarchy's values.
ch.file: Desktop stores only what you change, in {path}.
sec.monitors.d: Resolution, refresh rate, size, position and rotation of each display, and when it idles.
sec.keyboard.d: Keyboard language, Compose key and key repeat.
sec.cursor.d: Theme, size, when it hides and magnifier.
o.m:scale.d: Makes everything bigger (text, windows, bar) on displays without their own scale. Same scale as Omarchy's shortcut.
o.misc:vrr.d: Avoids tearing in games and video if the display supports it.
o.xwayland:force_zero_scaling.d: Stops X11 apps looking blurry when scaling (they may look smaller).
mon.title: Display {name}
mon.label: {name}: {field}
mon.mode.d: Image size and how many times per second it refreshes.
mon.scale.d: Size of everything shown on this display.
mon.position.d: Where this display is relative to the others (to move the mouse between them).
mon.transform.d: For displays mounted vertically or upside down.
note.no_global_scale: Your monitors.lua no longer has Omarchy's general scale: use each display's scale.
note.no_monitors: No displays detected: open Desktop inside your session to configure them.
o.input:kb_layout.d: Key layout. Separate several with commas to switch between them (e.g. us,es).
o.input:kb_variant.d: Fine-tunes the layout (dead keys, Dvorak…). If unsure, leave it empty.
o.kbopt:grp.d: If you have several languages, which keys switch between them.
o.kbopt:compose.d: Types special characters and emoji (Compose then a sequence). The chosen key stops doing its usual job.
o.kbopt:compose=caps: Caps Lock (Omarchy; no longer locks caps)
o.input:kb_model.d: Physical keyboard type. Rarely needs changing.
o.input:kb_options.d: Compose key, language switching and other XKB options.
o.input:repeat_rate.d: How many times per second a held key repeats.
o.input:repeat_delay.d: Milliseconds to hold a key before it starts repeating.
o.input:numlock_by_default.d: The number pad types numbers as soon as you log in.
o.input:sensitivity.d: Further right, the pointer moves faster.
o.input:accel_profile.d: With acceleration, moving the mouse fast takes the pointer further.
o.input:scroll_factor.d: How far a page scrolls with each wheel step.
o.input:natural_scroll.d: Reverses the wheel: content follows your finger, like on a phone.
o.input:left_handed.d: Swaps the left and right buttons.
o.input:follow_mouse.d: Whether the window under the pointer gets focus when you hover it.
o.input:mouse_refocus.d: Refocuses the window when the mouse crosses its border.
o.input:touchpad:natural_scroll.d: Swiping two fingers up moves content up, like on a phone.
o.input:touchpad:scroll_factor.d: How far a page scrolls when swiping two fingers.
o.input:touchpad:tap-to-click.d: A light tap on the touchpad counts as a click.
o.input:touchpad:clickfinger_behavior.d: Pressing with two fingers is a right click; three, a middle click.
o.input:touchpad:disable_while_typing.d: Avoids accidental palm clicks while typing.
o.x:ws_swipe.d: Swipe three fingers sideways on the touchpad to switch workspace.
o.input:touchpad:drag_3fg.d: Move windows or select text by swiping three fingers.
o.cursor:inactive_timeout.d: The pointer disappears after a few seconds without moving.
o.cursor:hide_on_key_press.d: The pointer hides when you type and comes back when you move the mouse.
o.cursor:zoom_factor.d: Magnifies the area around the pointer (1 = off).
o.cursor:hide_on_touch.d: The pointer hides when you touch the screen.
o.cursor:zoom_rigid.d: The magnified area moves with the pointer instead of following smoothly.
o.cursor:warp_on_change_workspace.d: Moves the pointer to the active window of the workspace you switch to.
o.cursor:no_hardware_cursors.d: Draws the pointer in software. Use it if it flickers or disappears.
sec.keybinds.d: Change, disable or add key combinations.
sec.autostart.d: Programs that open by themselves when you log in.
note.binds_offline: Open Desktop inside your Hyprland session to see and change shortcuts.
bind.search.hint: Type part of the name or keys (e.g. “terminal” or “SUPER + T”). Empty = show all.
bind.added: Shortcut added. Press Apply to use it.
bind.kind.title: What does {keys} do?
bind.kind.cmd.d: For advanced users: any terminal command.
bind.kind.web.d: Opens as a web app, in its own window.
rec.title: Record combination
rec.hint: Press the shortcut keys and release them. Escape cancels. Meanwhile, other shortcuts are paused.
rec.offline: To record shortcuts, open Desktop inside your Hyprland session.
rec.only_mods: A combination needs at least one key besides Super, Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
rec.conflict.title: Those keys are already in use
rec.conflict.d: If you continue, that shortcut will be disabled.
hint.bind: click to change keys, disable it or restore it
note.autostart: Programs that open when you log in (your autostart.lua). Omarchy's own services aren't listed and always start.
as.custom.d: Type the command to run at login.
restore.binds.desc: Shortcuts go back to Omarchy's and the ones you added here are removed.
restore.autostart.desc: Unapplied startup changes are undone. What's already saved is kept.
sec.nightlight.d: Tints the screen warm at night to be easier on your eyes.
sec.compose.d: Type long texts (your email, signature…) with just a few letters.
o.n:on.d: Starts with your session and changes the screen colour on schedule.
o.n:start.d: Time at which the screen starts to warm up.
o.n:end.d: Time at which the screen goes back to normal.
o.n:temp.d: The lower the number, the more orange the screen looks.
note.compose: Press your Compose key (chosen in Keyboard), then Space and the shortcut letters, and the text is typed. Only simple shortcuts of your ~/.XCompose are shown; the rest of the file is untouched.
xc.none: You have no text shortcuts yet.
xc.label: Compose, Space, {keys}
xc.desc: Text that gets typed. Enter to change it.
xc.keys.hint: The shortcut's letters or digits, without spaces (e.g. “nm” for your name). Up to 8.
xc.keys.err: Use only letters and digits, no spaces (up to 8).
xc.exists: You already have a shortcut with those letters.
xc.text.title: Text for {keys}
xc.text.hint: The text that will be typed when you use the shortcut.
restore.night.desc: Unapplied night light changes are undone.
restore.compose.desc: Unapplied changes are undone. What's already saved is kept.
mig.title: Import your Meca settings
mig.body:
Meca HyprConfig still stores settings that override Desktop's.
Desktop can import what you changed (and your shortcuts), keep a backup and stop loading Meca's file. You won't see any change on your desktop afterwards.
Import now?
mig.done: Imported: {n} settings and {b} shortcuts. Meca no longer overrides Desktop.
mig.failed: Could not import; nothing was changed:
mig.nothing: There are no Meca settings to import.
cli.migrate: import Meca settings and retire them
sec.language.d: Choose the computer's language: Lizarbe apps, the Omarchy menu and the system (dates and applications).
o.lg:ui.d: Applies to Desktop, Widgets and the menu. The system language changes after you log in again. Omarchy's bar and widgets stay in English.
lang.err_menu: Could not translate the Omarchy menu (lizarbe-menu-sync). Run lizarbe-doctor --fix.
lang.err_system: Could not change the system language (a password is requested to do it). The menu and apps did change.
hint.close: Close Desktop (asks if there are unapplied changes)
sec.screenshots.d: Where screenshots are saved, what the Print Screen key does and which editor opens them.
g.cap_save: Where and how they are saved
o.x:cap_dir.d: Where the images are saved. It is created on the first capture if missing.
o.x:cap_proc: What to do with the capture
o.x:cap_proc.d: Save the file, copy it to the clipboard, or both.
o.x:cap_mode.d: What the capture key offers: whatever you pick with the mouse (smart), a region, a window or the whole screen.
o.x:cap_editor.d: Opens when you click the capture notice. It must be installed.
o.x:cap_recdir.d: Where screen recording videos are saved.
cap.relogin: The folder and editing program already apply to the capture key; in the rest of the system (the Capture menu) they change the next time you log in.
note.gdk_mismatch: Your GTK and XWayland apps (Steam, Minecraft launchers…) use a different scale than the display, so they look huge or tiny. Apply changes to fix it.
gdk.relogin: The new scale for GTK and XWayland apps (Steam, Minecraft…) takes effect the next time you log in.
sec.system.d: Default apps, power, text size, printers, games, restore points, and shortcuts to network, Bluetooth and sound.
sys.instant: These changes take effect right away; no need to press Apply.
sys.no_options: There are no installed options to choose from.
sys.repair.d: If something stops working, restart it. It may ask for your password.
sys.failed: The command finished with an error.
snap.missing: Restore points need snapper, which is not installed.
snap.unconfigured: Snapper is installed but not configured: updates don't save a restore point.
snap.ready: Omarchy saves a restore point before every update.
snap.setup.confirm:
Omarchy's snapper setup will run in the terminal and ask for your password.
After that, every update will save a restore point.
undo.d: Every time you apply changes, Desktop keeps a copy of how the files were before.
undo.none: There are no changes to undo yet.
undo.pending: You have unapplied changes: apply or cancel them first.
undo.confirm:
Settings will go back to how they were right before the change from {when}.
What you have now is saved first, so you can undo this too.
undo.done: Done: settings are back to before the change from {when}.
snap.how_restore: To go back to a point: restart, choose “Snapshots” in the boot menu and pick the point you want. If everything works, come back here to keep it.
snap.in_snapshot: You started from a restore point. If everything works, keep it; if not, restart and the system goes back to how it was.
snap.keep.confirm:
The system will stay as it is in this restore point, also after restarting.
The terminal will open and ask for your password.
Your personal files (home folder) are not touched.
print.missing: The printing service (CUPS) is not installed.
print.disabled: The printing service is off: printers won't work.
print.no_app: Install “system-config-printer” from the store to add printers.
games.d: Omarchy installs Steam, Xbox controllers, Lutris, Heroic and more, with the drivers they need.
o.i:screensaver.d: Idle time before the screensaver starts.
o.i:lock.d: Idle time before the session locks (counted from when idle began). If shorter than the screensaver time, it locks first.
o.i:apps.d: While a browser or player shows a video, the screensaver and lock wait, like on other systems.
o.i:awake.d: Disables the screensaver and lock until you turn it off (the coffee cup in the Omarchy menu).
idle.apps_restart: Restart your browser so video apps pick up the new sleep setting.
